Definition: apparently akin to G4632 and G4639; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively):--habitation, tabernacle.
BiblicalUsage: Skene is the tabernacle, the tent, the dwelling place of God, and it moves from the wilderness to heaven. The fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, Christ is the minister of the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched and not man, and the great voice says the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tent is God's way of saying He lives with His people. He pitched it in the wilderness, He pitched it in Christ, and I hold that one day the tent will be our home forever.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
